Residuals of the joint subscore table for the Martin-Löf test

Source: R/martin_lof.R
RMdimMartinLofResiduals.Rd

Standardised residuals for each cell of the joint table of subscores, compared with its distribution under unidimensionality (Christensen, Bjorner, Kreiner, & Petersen, 2002, eq. 13). RMdimMartinLof() tests whether a partition departs from unidimensionality, and this table shows where.

Usage

RMdimMartinLofResiduals(
  data,
  partition,
  output = c("kable", "dataframe", "ggplot"),
  flag_threshold = NULL,
  color_by = c("residual", "n"),
  color_limits = NULL,
  min_expected = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame or matrix of item responses, items scored from 0. Only complete cases on the items in partition are used. Missing values on other items are ignored.

partition

As in RMdimMartinLof(): a list of item-name or index vectors, or a vector of length ncol(data) with each item's subscale. Each subscale must have at least 2 items.

output

Character. "kable" (default) for a two-way residual table when D = 2 (a long table when D > 2), "dataframe" for the long data.frame, or "ggplot" for a heatmap (D = 2, or D = 3 with a panel per value of t3, an error for D > 3).

flag_threshold

Numeric or NULL. If set, cells with |residual| > flag_threshold are marked, in bold in the kable and in a Flagged column of the data.frame. Default NULL, no marks: a fixed value is not a calibrated test, and with many cells some large residuals are expected under unidimensionality. RMdimMartinLof() is the test.

color_by

Character. What the tile colour shows with output = "ggplot". "residual" (default), a diverging red-white-blue scale centred at 0. "n", a sequential blue scale of the observed cell count, which shows whether large residuals come from sparse cells. In both, the residual is printed in each cell.

color_limits

Numeric vector of length 2, or NULL. Limits of the colour scale with output = "ggplot". Default c(-5, 5) with color_by = "residual", since residuals in cells with tiny expected counts can be very large and would compress the rest of the scale. The cell labels show the values without the limits. NULL with color_by = "n", which uses the range of the data.

min_expected

Numeric or NULL. If set, cells with an expected count below min_expected get the residual NA (grey in the heatmap, never flagged). Default NULL. A value of 1 or 5 is the analogue of the Cochran rule for sparse cells in chi-square tests, and removes residuals whose normal approximation is unreliable.

Value

  • output = "kable": a knitr_kable object. For D = 2, a wide table with t1 in rows, t2 in columns and the standardised residual in the cells (bold if beyond flag_threshold, a dash if NA). For D > 2, one row per cell.

  • output = "dataframe": a data.frame with one row per cell and the columns t1, ..., tD, total, observed, expected and residual, plus Flagged when flag_threshold is set.

  • output = "ggplot": a geom_tile() heatmap (D = 2 or 3 only).

Details

For each cell of the joint subscore table (indexed by \((t_1, \ldots, t_D)\)), the conditional probability under H0 given the total score \(t = \sum_d t_d\) is $$p(t_1, \ldots, t_D \mid t) = \prod_d \gamma^{(d)}_{t_d} / \gamma_t,$$ the expected count is \(e = n_t \cdot p\), and the residual is \((o - e) / \sqrt{n_t \cdot p \cdot (1 - p)}\). CML estimates from the unidimensional model are used for the \(\gamma\)-functions.

Reading the table (D = 2): under unidimensionality, the residuals should show no pattern and be roughly N(0, 1). Multidimensionality with positively correlated dimensions typically shows up as positive residuals at the corners of each antidiagonal (high t1 + low t2, low t1 + high t2) and negative residuals near the antidiagonal centre (matched subscores). Negatively correlated dimensions show positive residuals at the table corners (high/low and low/high) and negative residuals at high/high and low/low. See Christensen et al. (2002, section 7) for a worked example.

Cells where the total score has no observed cases (n_t = 0) are uninformative and are dropped from the output.

Complete cases only, as in RMdimMartinLof, and rows with NA are dropped only after items outside partition have been removed. The reported n = X of Y respondents counts respondents complete on the partitioned items against the raw input rows.

Expected counts and residuals agree to numerical precision with the pml SAS macro (Christensen, 2004), kindly shared by Karl Bang Christensen. The one deliberate difference is at the extreme totals t = 0 and t = max, where the conditional probability is 1 and the residual is undefined: the macro prints 0, this function returns NA.

References

Christensen, K. B. (2004). pml: A SAS macro for testing unidimensionality in polytomous Rasch models (Technical note). National Institute of Occupational Health, Denmark, and Department of Biostatistics, University of Copenhagen.

Christensen, K. B., Bjorner, J. B., Kreiner, S., & Petersen, J. H. (2002). Testing unidimensionality in polytomous Rasch models. Psychometrika, 67(4), 563-574. doi:10.1007/BF02295131

See also

RMdimMartinLof()

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(1)
dat <- as.data.frame(matrix(sample(0:1, 400 * 8, replace = TRUE),
                            nrow = 400, ncol = 8))
colnames(dat) <- paste0("I", 1:8)

# Wide kable table for D = 2
RMdimMartinLofResiduals(dat,
                     partition = list(c("I1","I2","I3","I4"),
                                      c("I5","I6","I7","I8")))
#> Warning: NaNs produced
#> 
#> 
#> Table: Standardised residuals (Christensen et al. 2002, eq. 13). Rows = subscale 1 score, columns = subscale 2 score. -- = uncomputable. n = 400 respondents.
#> 
#> |t1\t2 |0     |1     |2     |3     |4     |
#> |:-----|:-----|:-----|:-----|:-----|:-----|
#> |0     |      |0.95  |2.38  |-0.32 |-1.31 |
#> |1     |-0.95 |-2.17 |-0.12 |0.32  |0.22  |
#> |2     |0.22  |0.11  |-0.41 |0.10  |0.84  |
#> |3     |0.35  |0.22  |-0.46 |-0.66 |-1.67 |
#> |4     |1.22  |0.47  |-0.06 |1.67  |--    |

# Heatmap
if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  RMdimMartinLofResiduals(dat,
                       partition = c(1,1,1,1,2,2,2,2),
                       output = "ggplot")
}
#> Warning: NaNs produced


# Underlying data.frame for custom analysis
df <- RMdimMartinLofResiduals(dat,
                           partition = c(1,1,1,1,2,2,2,2),
                           flag_threshold = 2,
                           output = "dataframe")
#> Warning: NaNs produced
df[df$Flagged, ]
#>   t1 t2 total observed expected  residual Flagged
#> 3  0  2     2       18 11.02774  2.378139    TRUE
#> 4  1  1     2       21 28.59561 -2.170933    TRUE
# }
